Description

After injury spinal microglia express the ATP-gated channel P2X4. ATP opens it, and the calcium that enters activates p38 MAP kinase, which drives the synthesis and release of BDNF. Microglial BDNF acts on TrkB of lamina I neurons and weakens their inhibition. The pathway was described after nerve injury and is male-specific in rodents. In OA models spinal microglia are activated after intra-articular monoiodoacetate and after destabilisation of the medial meniscus.

Colour

Each block is coloured by its effect on pain, red where it raises pain and blue where it relieves it, and everything in it takes that colour, GTP and GDP included, as it works for the block's result. Drugs are yellow and classes of molecules white.

This block is red: P2X4 and BDNF lead to the loss of inhibition.
